title: Emily Brontë's birth chart
metaDescription: Emily Brontë's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 6.6° Leo. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Sun stands at 6.6° Leo, in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's exact place is 6.6° Leo. That falls in the first decan, 0°–10°, sub-ruled by the Sun in the classical scheme — a fire sign read through a fixed season.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The tightest geometry in the chart puts Venus in the same degree of the zodiac from Mars, 0.3° off exact. Two bodies in the same degree are not read as neighbours but as a merger: whatever one wants, the other is already funding. Behind it, Saturn square Uranus at 1.0°, and Neptune square Pluto at 2.2° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, four sit in a sign it has an opinion about. The Sun in Leo at 6.6° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; the Moon in Cancer at 6.6° is in domicile; Venus in Virgo at 12.1° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Jupiter in Capricorn at 4.6° is in fall. The table describes circumstance rather than quality — a planet in detriment is inconvenienced, not diminished.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: By element the ten bodies divide 4 fire, 3 water, 3 earth; by modality, 6 mutable, 2 fixed, 2 cardinal. Fire signs carry the scheme’s forward pressure: heat applied early, patience treated as a later skill. No body at all in air — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — the backward drift a body appears to make as the Earth overtakes it, read in the scheme as a function that reviews before it releases.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Cancer for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 12.0° between midnight and midnight. That is quick enough to make the exact degree a neighbourhood rather than an address, and slow enough to leave the sign settled. At the noon reference it stands at 6.6°.
